The window is, of course, of a set length, let's say small omega. And when the window slides on this sequence, this binary sequence, of course it creates smaller size binary codes. Now our memory and numbers are using binary encoding to be represented. Which means that when one window slides on this sequence, depending on which part of the sequence the window reads, it produces a new number. And under the condition that the binary sequence on which the window slides can be fully scanned by the window with a number that can be expressed in bits that is slower, that is lower than the final number we can represent when you concatenate the results of the window reading the original binary sequence and sliding on it, then what we have is that we have encoded, we have compressed information because we have a way to generate bigger numbers by sliding the window on this original binary sequence.
